convoLines.text: "I asked Maricela about what happened to my taken kin — Maricela's gone. You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Joseph?"
They nod. "Okay."
The mood shifts, subtly.

"It's my uncle, Joseph. Was taken. He could fix anything. Anything. I wonder what they even measure. The pods get into my sleep some nights. Row on row of them, humming like a held note -- and I wake up reaching for something that isn't there."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Gotta keep moving."
"This one — Maypop. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Fish Mint. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Have you heard what they're calling Lockpick? I'm pushing 'The Big Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. I wanted to ask rather than assume."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it?"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Nora shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"The whole fire was arguing about Lockpick last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Loud Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I should let you go. Be well, okay?"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet."
Nadia has an edge today — something curdled.
"Why do you ask? Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that."
"Have you heard what they're calling Lockpick? Tyler is pushing 'The Big Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Nora grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Nadia is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"Still on what's been happening. Doesn't matter now."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About what happened to my taken kin — Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all. Can't sit still, you know?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Still nothing on Joseph. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The whole fire was arguing about Glasswing Darter last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big Ugly' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Nadia nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Give it three more days of arguing. Then someone says the obvious thing and we all pretend it was theirs."
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Permit me: We never finished talking about grief — we wandered off it, 4 days back. 'They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything.'"
Nora has an edge today — something curdled.
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
A pause that's a beat too long. "I think you're confused," Nora says, not quite looking at you.
A long exhale. "I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
Tyler nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that. That is all."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You're one of the good ones. Don't make me regret saying that out loud." "That's where we are."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"This was good." They mean it.

lines: d6: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d6: 🕯️ Maricela Holmes is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d6: What Maricela kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d6: Joyce picks up the journal. Their hands shake. Then they open it, and keep writing.

d6: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Research & Records (Level 1). Find information fast: indexes, archives, and asking the right question.
d6: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d6: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Maricela Holmes, 6 days. The mantle passes to Joyce Weber.
d6: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Joyce Weber, 39 — a librarian. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm.
d6: The fire knew Joyce — solid ground, earned at this fire.

lastSay: d16: (217 kcal of dried meat and clean water. Nothing traceable.)
d16: 🔥 Oliver says it at the fire, not quite looking at Nora: “Your trade story doesn’t add up. Someone had to say it.” The fire goes quiet in the way it does when someone’s decided to be brave.
d16: “You’re right.” Nora doesn’t look up. “I wasn’t truck driver. I was tailor. I’m sorry — I wanted a cleaner story than I had.” The fire lets it land. Someone passes Nora the bowl without a word.
d16: Tyler Braun reads the sky: frost tomorrow, cold.
d16: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. By the fire. Good enough.)
